name: Delaware River–Turnpike Toll Bridge
facts: The Delaware River–Turnpike Toll Bridge, completed in 1956, was engineered as a high-level steel through arch to keep traffic moving nonstop, contrasting sharply with downstream drawbridges that open for ship traffic.

In 2013, a 2011 investigation revealed aging suspenders on the main span; engineers replaced each 4‑inch wire rope with four 2‑inch ropes, restoring the bridge’s structural integrity after decades of service.
On January 20, 2017, a 1‑inch crack in an I‑beam 80 feet above ground caused a 1‑inch drop, prompting emergency steel plates and a swift repair that reopened the bridge by March 9, 2017.
